title: Mathematics AI SL · Set B · Paper 1

questions.stem: A device stores 7.2 × 10⁹ bytes of observations in a day. Each full archive block stores exactly 3.0 × 10⁶ bytes. For this calculation take the quoted values as exact.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the number of full blocks required for one day. Give your answer in ordinary notation.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Compression is expected to save 18% of the bytes, but the actual saving could be from 16% to 20%, inclusive. Find the smallest guaranteed sufficient number of blocks and explain your choice of percentage.

steps.text: The smallest saving gives the largest file, so use 16%.
This already is a whole number; any smaller allocation fails at the 16% endpoint.

questions.stem: A battery delivers 84 km of range when new. At each annual inspection its measured range is modelled as 93% of the previous inspection's range.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the model after n annual intervals and find the predicted range after three.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Replacement is required at the first inspection when range is below 55 km. Determine which inspection triggers replacement, justifying the integer choice.

steps.text: Compare the model with 55, using a table or solving for n.
It first falls below 55 at inspection 6 because the sequence decreases.

questions.stem: From a lookout, an observer sights a buoy on a bearing of 040° and a second buoy on a bearing of 105°. The buoys are 2.8 km and 4.1 km from the lookout respectively.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the included angle and the distance between the buoys.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A boat travels directly from the first buoy to the second at 12 km/h. Find the time in minutes. Explain why the result might underestimate the actual time.

steps.text: A detour around a shoal or an opposing current could increase time; accept an appropriate contextual reason.

questions.stem: Forty calls are grouped by duration t minutes. The frequencies for 0 ≤ t < 2, 2 ≤ t < 4, 4 ≤ t < 8 and 8 ≤ t < 12 are 6, 14, 12 and 8.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Estimate the mean call duration.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What fraction of calls lasted at least 4 minutes? Explain why this is exact for the sample although your mean is an estimate.

steps.text: The threshold lies on a class boundary, so every call can be counted on the correct side.
The mean used midpoints in place of the unknown individual durations.

questions.stem: The height of a launched water jet is h(t) = 0.8 + 6t − 4.9t² metres, where t is time in seconds after launch. The model ends when the jet first reaches the ground.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the maximum height and the time at which it occurs.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine the model's time domain, and explain why the other algebraic zero is excluded.

steps.text: Use the maximum of the quadratic on t ≥ 0.
The other root is before launch and outside the physical experiment.

questions.stem: A factory models fill mass X by a normal distribution of mean 506 g and standard deviation 3.8 g. Underweight packs have mass below 500 g.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly selected pack is underweight.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the 95th percentile of mass. A supervisor claims exactly 5 packs in every batch of 100 will exceed that mass. Comment.

steps.text: Use the lower normal tail with mean 506 and standard deviation 3.8.
Use inverse normal with lower area 0.95.
A randomly selected pack has probability 0.05 of exceeding this threshold.
Five is an expected number, not an exact batch count.

questions.stem: Five film clips P, Q, R, S and T receive two sets of ranks (1 = best). The youth panel ranks them 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; the adult panel ranks them 2, 4, 1, 3, 5, in the same clip order.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate Spearman's rank correlation coefficient.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain why ranking observations can hide information. Does the coefficient show that both panels chose the same winner?

steps.text: Use 1 − 6 × 10/[5(5² − 1)], or correlation of the two rank lists.
Rankings discard the gaps in actual scores.
No; a positive coefficient describes overall association, not identical first choices.
The youth panel selects P, while the adult panel selects R.

questions.stem: A cylindrical sample tube has internal radius 1.6 cm and a straight usable length of 11 cm. It may be filled to only 85% of its cylindrical volume. Treat the stated dimensions and fill fraction as exact in this model. Use 1 cm³ = 1 mL.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine its permitted liquid volume.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A technician must store 1.88 litres. Find the minimum number of tubes, and explain why rounding the capacity first to the nearest 10 mL could give a different decision.

steps.text: Convert to 1880 mL and divide by the unrounded permitted capacity.
The quotient is approximately 25.001; 25 tubes hold only about 1879.93 mL.
Rounding each capacity to 80 mL overstates the total and could suggest only 24 tubes.

questions.stem: Two mobile clinics are at U(−2, 1) and V(4, 1). All coordinates are in kilometres; travel is modelled along straight lines.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the boundary between their nearest-clinic regions. Explain why it is vertical.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A river makes the actual journey from P(0, 3) to U twice the straight-line distance, while the journey to V equals its straight-line distance. Determine which clinic is now closer by journey distance.

steps.text: UV is horizontal; its perpendicular bisector is vertical.
Straight distances to U and V are √8 and √20.
The straight-line boundary would have assigned P to U because x < 1; the river breaks the model assumption.

questions.stem: At a fair a player pays 4 dollars and receives exactly one gross prize: 0 dollars with probability 0.60, 5 dollars with probability 0.30 or 20 dollars otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability of the largest prize and the expected net gain to the player.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The fair keeps the fee and probabilities fixed. Find the largest prize that would make the game fair, and explain what fair means here.

steps.text: Let the new top prize be k. Set expected net gain to zero.
Fair means zero expected net gain over repeated plays, not that every player breaks even.

questions.stem: The energy E in a small thermal store after t hours is modelled by E(t) = 18 + 8t − t² kWh, for 0 ≤ t ≤ 5.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find E(2) and the slope of the tangent to the graph at t = 2.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use the tangent to estimate E(2.5), and calculate the error in your estimate.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain geometrically why the same tangent also overestimates E(1.5).

steps.text: The graph is concave down on the interval.
It lies below its tangent on both sides of t = 2, apart from the contact point.

questions.stem: Independent random samples of delivery times are taken for two firms. Assume approximately normal populations. A two-sided independent-samples t-test of equal population means returns p = 0.031.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State both hypotheses in the context of this study.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: State the decision and its contextual conclusion at 5%, then explain what changes at 1%.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why the reported p-value alone cannot establish which firm is faster or whether the difference matters to customers.

steps.text: H0: the firms have equal population mean delivery times.
H1: their population mean delivery times differ.
Reject H0 at 5%; there is evidence of a difference in the firms' population means.
At 1% do not reject H0; the evidence is insufficient at that level.
A two-sided p-value has no direction; compare the observed means to establish the sample direction.
It does not give the size of the time difference; assess a difference in minutes against a meaningful threshold.
